clue.text: Add to enclosure containing buildings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to make a problem worse by adding to it
second meaning: a fenced area holding a group of buildings

explanation.surface: Someone is extending a walled yard by putting up more buildings inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one instruction, but it splits after 'Add to': a verb meaning to worsen, and a noun for a fenced site.
explanation.definitionFit: To compound a difficulty is to increase it, and a compound is also a walled area with houses or factories inside.

clue.text: Old tips for restoring an instrument

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of restoring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shares advice on how to repair an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice, but it means the end letters of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a keyboard instrument, sounded by air through pipes, found in churches.

clue.text: Delighted with sale, chap ends up getting tipsy

indicators.note: someone tipsy staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch out of order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man thrilled with a bargain ends up drunk celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends up' looks like it is about last letters, but those words are simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, after the always-grinning puppet Mr Punch, means extremely happy or delighted.

clue.text: Crude vote, nearly held by university, dropped

indicators.note: what is held by something sits gripped inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: uni is short for university

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a poll is a vote; its last letter goes
shed means dropped or cast off

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready ballot at a university was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpolished is unrefined or rough, lacking finish, which is the sense of crude here.

clue.text: Five hundred on vessel without light

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Five hundred people are aboard a ship sailing with no lights.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark describes a place or time with no illumination, unlit and shadowy.

clue.text: Stare at Oscar with endless joy

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the following word is dropped
with means accompanied by, so the two pieces simply sit side by side

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
glee is joy; the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at a man called Oscar with boundless delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle someone is to look at them fixedly, usually with obvious desire, which is staring.

clue.text: See about run, refreshed after drink and biscuit

indicators.note: coming after something means placed behind it, so the drink goes first in the answer

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to get something is to see or understand it

indicators.note: something refreshed has been revived and made over, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: After a jog, someone revived with a drink and a cookie.
explanation.walkthrough: Get as in 'I get it' means see. A ginger nut is a hard ginger biscuit popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a crisp, ginger-flavoured British cookie, so it is one kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Sign up in street topped with funny line

indicators.note: in a down entry, being topped with something puts that thing above, so it comes first
something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters come out strangely arranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A recruiting post on a street carries a humorous slogan to attract volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'topped with' puts the rearranged letters above the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join up or enrol, especially in the armed forces, which is signing up.

clue.text: Mischief aboard vital vehicle popular during disorder

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the run of short words goes inside the last piece

parts.note: a mess is disorder
on means aboard, as in on the bus
key means vital or essential
a bus is a vehicle
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Pranks on board a crucial, well-loved vehicle cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short words are strung together and the whole string sits inside the word for disorder, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for playful or underhand behaviour, the sort of trickery called mischief.

clue.text: Fish in perspective

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to fish with rod and line
second meaning: a point of view taken on a subject

explanation.surface: A fish is seen from a certain viewpoint, like a still life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'in' just links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers fish with a hook, and an angle is also a slant or viewpoint from which something is considered.

clue.text: Horrified tourist's latest story coming up, about hotel

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the latest part of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of tourist

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed string goes round the hotel letter

parts.note: a saga is a long story
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller is appalled by the latest tale about the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock or horror, struck dumb by something dreadful.

clue.text: Staff thus after end of seminar tucked into pasta and left

indicators.note: placed after means behind, so the selected letter comes before the word for thus
something tucked into a thing is pushed inside it, so these letters go within the pasta

parts.note: penne is a tube-shaped pasta

indicators.note: and simply adds the next piece on at the end
the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept here

parts.note: the last letter of seminar
so means thus, in this way
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: At a seminar's close, food is tucked into and leftovers abandoned by the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: RSO goes inside the pasta after its second letter, then L is added to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, which is what its staff means collectively.

clue.text: Pious in retreat? On the contrary, in truth

indicators.note: in means inside, so one word is placed within the other
this flips the stated order, so the second word goes inside the first rather than the other way round

parts.note: holy means devout or pious
a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Is a devout person really living in seclusion? No, it is the other way round, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'Pious in retreat' would put the holy word inside the other; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so the retreat goes inside the pious word.
explanation.definitionFit: Honestly is used as an adverb meaning truly or really, the same sense as the phrase in truth.

clue.text: Captains ignoring very quiet competitors in winter sport?

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: skippers are captains of ships or teams
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: Team captains overlook the silent rivals at a winter games event.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the music notation pianissimo. The question mark flags that the definition is a description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: People racing downhill or cross-country on snow are among the athletes who compete at winter sports.

clue.text: Page on garden in preliminary survey getting priority

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the page letter comes first

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page

indicators.note: in means inside, so the garden goes within the survey word

parts.note: a recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting survey
Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A page in a preliminary garden report is given top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: Recce is British informal for a reconnaissance. In a down entry, 'on' puts the page letter above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedence is the right to come first in order or importance, which is the meaning of priority.

clue.text: Monotonous style ruins good broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dull presentation manner spoils a decent radio or television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Work so tedious and repetitive that it crushes the spirit is described with this hyphenated phrase, a strong word for monotonous.

clue.text: United in due course to protect large south-western lake

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it by surrounding it, so one word wraps around others

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
later means in due course, eventually
L is the abbreviation for large
SW is the abbreviation for south-western

explanation.surface: A football club will eventually help conserve a big lake in the southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullswater is a large lake in England's Lake District, in the north-west, so the 'south-western' in the surface is a misleading touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullswater is the second-largest body of water in the English Lake District, so it is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Shaft of light in trick becoming stick of wax?

indicators.note: in means inside, so the beam goes within the word for trick

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a ray is a beam or shaft of light

explanation.surface: A beam of light in a magic trick seems to turn into a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the drawing stick is coloured wax rather than a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a coloured stick of wax used for drawing, especially by children.

clue.text: Observed disc following fool with no time for UFO sighting?

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the named letter is taken out of the word
following means coming after, so the shortened word goes first

parts.note: a clot is a fool, in British slang
T is the abbreviation for time
seen means observed
a counter is a small disc used in board games

explanation.surface: Someone saw a flying saucer just after a silly person wasted no time, a supposed alien sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The disc looks like a flying saucer but is a counter from a board game. Clot is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, popularised by the Spielberg film title, describes an alleged meeting with or sighting of aliens or their craft.

clue.text: Assurance in place with advantage

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two pieces simply join end to end

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an edge is an advantage over rivals

explanation.surface: A guarantee is in place, giving someone the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or guarantee, the kind of assurance given to reassure someone.

clue.text: Player's second foul allowed

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the word, which alone is kept

parts.note: the second letter of player
awful means foul, very unpleasant

explanation.surface: A footballer's second foul of the match is let go by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sporting infringement, but 'second' picks one letter and 'foul' is an adjective for nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful is permitted by law, so the adjective means legally allowed.

clue.text: Consultative volume is probing trouble with railway

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the last piece is added on at the end
a probe pushes inside something, so these pieces go within the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
V is the abbreviation for volume
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A book of advice investigates problems on the railways.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisory body gives advice and is consulted rather than deciding, so it is consultative in role.

clue.text: Upset about supporting bad proposal

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports sits underneath, so the turned word comes last

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so in a down entry the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about backing a poor plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' puts the reversed word underneath the word for bad.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is something put forward for acceptance, such as a bid, which is a proposal.

clue.text: Reportedly avoided thin fog

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: missed means avoided, as in narrowly missed

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a driver steered clear of a light haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is fine water droplets in the air, a haze lighter than fog, so a thin fog.

clue.text: Discovery coming from confinement with carbon instead of nitrogen

indicators.note: instead of means in place of, so one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: detention is confinement, being held in custody
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A finding emerges from a chemistry experiment run in isolation, swapping one element for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first N in the word for confinement becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: Detection is the act of finding out or noticing something hidden, which is discovery.

clue.text: Rebel finally, to some extent, impish

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A rebel at last turns out to be somewhat mischievous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like a last-letter signal, but it is just the word the letters run into.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, small and mischievous, close to impish, like an imp.

clue.text: Study without large merit

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to learn is to study
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Studying without great effort deserves credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to deserve it by one's efforts, the verb sense of merit.

clue.text: Meal about right with definite value

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the last word is added on at the end
about means around, so the meal wraps around the single letter

parts.note: tea is an evening or afternoon meal in Britain
R is the abbreviation for right
sure means certain, definite

explanation.surface: A meal is reckoned to be good value for money.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can mean an early evening meal, not only the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value it highly, cherishing it as precious.
